title: ScaleFusion: Scalable Inference of Spatial-Temporal Diffusion Transformers for High-Resolution Long Video Generation
problem: Existing sequence parallelism techniques (DeepSpeed-Ulysses, RingAttention, DSP) for distributed ST-DiT inference incur 34-44% communication overhead when crossing machine boundaries, preventing efficient strong scaling beyond a single server.
motivation: Generating 1080p video with OpenSora ST-DiT (1.1B params) takes >5 minutes on a single A100 GPU. Multi-machine scaling is needed but ST-DiT's alternating spatial/temporal attention requires back-to-back all-to-all collectives (tensor re-sharding between spatial-distributed and temporal-distributed layouts) with serial data dependencies, making communication-computation overlap non-trivial. Cross-machine NVLink/NVSwitch bandwidth is unavailable; AWS EFA provides only 400 Gbps vs multi-TB/s NVSwitch intra-node.
method: ScaleFusion exploits spatial-temporal independence: spatial attention (comparing pixels across the image) is independent from different time frames, and temporal attention is independent from different spatial regions. This enables splitting each layer into 4 temporal or 4 spatial slices without breaking dependencies. Within a layer, it overlaps computation and communication: while computing slice i, it prepares the all-to-all data exchange for slice i+1. Between layers, it eliminates additional idle time by overlapping 2/3 of the next layer's data exchange with the previous layer's final slice, using two parallel execution streams with default parameters: 4 temporal slices, 4 spatial slices, 1 temporal sub-partition, and 3 spatial sub-partitions.
key_novelty: ScaleFusion eliminates cross-machine all-to-all communication overhead in spatial-temporal video transformers by overlapping these data exchanges with computation both within layers and between consecutive layers, exploiting the independence of spatial and temporal attention.
contributions: Identification and formal proof of spatial-temporal independence property in ST-DiT architectures
Intra-layer communication scheduling: pipeline all-to-all of slice i+1 with computation of slice i
Inter-layer communication scheduling: lift first-slice communication partitions to previous layer's last-slice computation window
Configurable NT, NS, LT, LS hyperparameters adapting to different video resolutions and durations
3.60x strong scaling on 32 A100 GPUs (4 machines) vs 8 GPUs; 97-103% weak scaling efficiency
1.36x average (up to 1.58x) speedup over DSP; 1.28x peak memory reduction vs OpenSora; avoids OOM at 4k resolution
hardware_target: NVIDIA A100 40GB GPUs; Amazon EC2 p4d.24xlarge instances; AWS EFA 400 Gbps cross-machine interconnect
baselines: DSP (Dynamic Sequence Parallelism, Zhao et al. 2024)
limitations: Hyperparameter tuning (NT, NS, LT, LS) requires profiling for new video resolutions or models
Inter-layer scheduling adds communication-ordering complexity and partial tensor re-arrangements
Limited to ST-DiT architectures with strict alternating spatial-temporal attention structure
